newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ELS IN HISTORIC THIRD STRAIGHT MATCHPLAY WIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS IN HISTORIC THIRD STRAIGHT MATCHPLAY WIN.

text.p: Ernie Els carved himself a slice of golfing history on Sunday when he became the first player to capture the World Matchplay title for a third succcessive year.

The 27-year-old South African top seed beat unseeded Fijian Vijay Singh 3 and 2, defying persistent afternoon rain to remain unbeaten at this event with nine match victories over the past three years.
The world number four's triumph earned him 170,000 pounds ($269,900) and brought his winnings from his three visits to the tournament to a massive 500,000 pounds ($793,900).
Singh, playing in his first final, won 90,000 pounds ($142,900).
Els led by two holes after 17 but lost the last morning hole and the first in the afternoon as Singh drew level.
But Els won the 22nd after Singh drove into trees and three birdies in four holes from the 24th put him in control.
"After the second hole this afternoon I did not play badly. It's a great feeling to win three times in a row," Els said.
In the third place playoff, U.S. PGA champion Mark Brooks beat British Open titleholder Tom Lehman by one hole.
